Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: No confirmed digital authentication function is available for the Mozambican national ID card. The BI is a physical card with fingerprint and photograph. The e-Government Development Index ranks Mozambique 173/193 (2023), indicating very limited e-government infrastructure. The SIGAV platform exists for passport scheduling but no online digital authentication via the national ID is documented. The EDGE project aims to develop digital authentication capabilities but this is not yet deployed.
revision_notes: Both cited sources fetched and read; neither documents an operational digital/electronic authentication function for the national ID (BI). No fresher evidence of a launched biometric-matching, PIN/OTP or QR-based verification service was found. Score of 1 (No) confirmed.
revised_comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) is a physical biometric card; no digital authentication function - such as online biometric matching, PIN/OTP or QR-code verification - is documented. Mozambique's e-Government Development Index ranking remains low, and the World Bank-backed EDGE project is developing digital authentication capabilities that are not yet deployed. The SIGAV platform supports online passport-appointment scheduling but does not provide identity authentication via the national ID.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No documented mechanism exists allowing individuals to view their own data held in the national ID database online. The Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017 grants individuals rights to access and correct their data, and the Constitution (Article 71) provides a right of access, but there is no operational portal or system enabling individuals to access their ID data digitally. The proposed draft data protection law would establish data subject rights including access, but this is not yet enacted.
revision_notes: Both cited sources fetched and read. DLA Piper (updated Feb 2026) confirms Mozambique still has no dedicated data protection law giving individuals a self-service data-access right, and a June 2025 UNECA inception report on Mozambique's forthcoming National Data Governance Strategy confirms the country still lacks a unified data governance framework and that a Data Protection Bill (with data-subject access rights) remains in draft. No operational self-service ID data portal was found. Score of 1 (No) confirmed with fresher evidence.
revised_comments: No mechanism allows individuals to view their own data held in the national ID database online. The 2004 Constitution (Article 71) and the Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017 provide general rights of access and correction, but no operational self-service portal exists. A draft Data Protection Bill, under development with UNECA/GIZ/AU support as part of a National Data Governance Strategy, would establish formal data-subject access rights, but this remains unenacted.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: General judicial oversight exists under Mozambique's constitution and legal system. The Constitution (2004) provides for rights protection and access to courts. DLA Piper confirms courts can issue orders regarding data access. However, there are no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms or specialized data protection tribunals. The draft data protection law proposes administrative enforcement by ANPD rather than judicial mechanisms. Oversight is not ID-specific.
revision_notes: Both cited sources fetched and read; confirm general constitutional and judicial oversight but no ID-specific judicial mechanism. Score of 2 (Yes, but not specific to ID) confirmed.
revised_comments: General judicial oversight of the ID system exists under Mozambique's constitutional and legal order; the 2004 Constitution provides for rights protection and access to the courts, and data protection sources confirm courts can issue orders concerning data access. There is no specialised, ID-specific judicial review mechanism or data protection tribunal; the draft Data Protection Bill proposes administrative enforcement through a future Data Protection Authority rather than judicial mechanisms.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial integration exists. The NUIC (Unique Citizen Identification Number) is assigned at birth and links the e-CRVS system with the national ID card. Birth certificates are prerequisites for obtaining NIDs. The UNICEF evaluation notes the 'e-CRVS system can still be better integrated with the national ID system.' INAE CRVS snapshot confirms GITEV inter-ministerial working group coordinates integration. The EDGE project (World Bank) is supporting further integration through single-window issuance. Full real-time automatic integration between CRVS and NID systems does not yet exist.
revision_notes: Cited sources fetched and read. Confirmed the NUIC (assigned at birth) links civil registration to the national ID, and a fresh search located Law No. 6/2022 (20 June 2022), which legally mandates that the Unico Numero de Identificacao Civil integrate civil registration, tax identification and social security numbers, plus an implementing decree approved by the Council of Ministers on 2 June 2026. No source confirms this legal integration is yet operational nationwide; UNICEF and UNECA sources continue to describe coordination gaps between CRVS and ID systems. Score of 2 (Partial integration) confirmed.
revised_comments: Integration between civil registration and the national ID is partial. The Unique Citizen Identification Number (NUIC), assigned at birth, links the e-CRVS system with the national ID card, and a birth certificate is a prerequisite for obtaining a BI. Law No. 6/2022 provides for the NUIC to integrate civil registration, tax identification and social security numbers, with an implementing decree approved by the Council of Ministers in June 2026, but full real-time, automated integration between the CRVS and national ID systems is not yet confirmed as operational; an inter-ministerial working group (GITEV) coordinates ongoing integration efforts, supported by the World Bank's EDGE project.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data sharing rules are partially available. The Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017 requires prior notification to INTIC for data processing and mandates consent for data transfers. The Constitution prohibits unauthorized access to and transfer of personal data (Article 71). Banking regulations (Notice 8/GBM/2021) require clear policies protecting consumer data. However, without a comprehensive data protection law and formal DPA, the framework is incomplete and not fully articulated for ID-specific data sharing. The EDGE project is developing a national data governance framework.
revision_notes: Original two sources fetched and read; both confirm Mozambique still lacks a comprehensive data protection law, consistent with 'partially available' rules based on the Electronic Transactions Law and constitutional provisions. A fresh search found that Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved, on 2 June 2026, a new decree ('Regime Juridico de Identificacao Civil e do Bilhete de Identidade') reportedly establishing clear rules for the collection, processing, management and retention of citizens' identification data. The decree had only just been approved at the time of writing, with no confirmation found that it has been gazetted, published in full, or entered into force, so it is not possible to confirm whether it meets the 'fully available' threshold. Flagged for human review pending confirmation of the decree's full text and entry-into-force date.
revised_comments: Data-sharing rules for the ID system are partially established. The Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017 requires notification to INTIC for data processing and consent for data transfers, and the Constitution prohibits unauthorised access to or transfer of personal data (Article 71). Mozambique still lacks a comprehensive data protection law and a functioning Data Protection Authority, so ID-specific data-sharing rules are not fully codified or publicly documented, though a new decree specifically regulating the collection, processing and retention of citizens' identification data was approved by the Council of Ministers in June 2026 and may extend the framework once it is in force.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: There is no standalone Digital ID-specific regulation in Mozambique. The biometric ID card is governed by Decree No.11/2008 (general identity card decree) and the NUIC by Decree 44/2010 but these are not comprehensive digital ID regulations. The country has a draft data protection bill and is developing a data governance framework under the EDGE project, but no dedicated digital ID law has been enacted as of 2023.
revision_notes: Original three sources fetched and read; confirm no standalone digital-ID law existed as of 2023-2025, only the general identity-card decree (11/2008) and NUIC decree (44/2010). A fresh search located Law No. 6/2022 and a new implementing decree approved by the Council of Ministers on 2 June 2026 specifically regulating the 'Regime Juridico de Identificacao Civil e do Bilhete de Identidade', explicitly aimed at strengthening security of 'digital and physical' identification documents. Whether this instrument meets the definition of digital-ID-specific regulation 'beyond general identification legislation' is genuinely unclear from the reporting available (it appears to remain an ID-card regulation rather than a separate digital-identity law), and the decree's full text/gazettal has not been located. Flagged for human review pending the decree's publication.
revised_comments: There is no standalone digital-ID-specific law distinct from general identification legislation. The biometric BI is governed by Decree No.11/2008 and the NUIC by Decree 44/2010, and Mozambique continues to develop a national data governance framework (with UNECA/GIZ/AU support, as of June 2025) rather than a dedicated digital ID law. A new decree regulating the civil identification and BI regime, aimed partly at strengthening digital identification document security, was approved by the Council of Ministers in June 2026, though its scope and legal status are not yet fully confirmed.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) serves as the primary legal proof of identity for Mozambican citizens before the law. Multiple sources confirm it is required for voting, banking, accessing education, employment, health services, and formal transactions. The Global Protection Cluster briefing note (2021) states that without the BI, 'several obstacles to exercise basic rights arise, such as: to move freely, to vote, to access education, employment, healthcare, bank services.' The NUIC issued at birth is the foundational legal identifier.
revision_notes: Both sources fetched and read; confirm the BI is required for a wide range of civic and economic activities and functions as the primary legal identity document. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed.
revised_comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) is the primary legal proof of identity for Mozambican citizens. It is required to vote, open bank accounts, access education and healthcare services, and undertake formal employment and transactions. Without it, individuals face significant obstacles exercising basic rights. The NUIC, assigned at birth, underpins the citizen's foundational legal identity.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Legal framework exists across multiple instruments: Decree No.11/2008 regulating the biometric identity card; Decree 44/2010 establishing the Unique Citizen Identification Number (NUIC); Civil Registration Code 12/2018 (enacted December 2018) providing the framework for civil registration and electronic CRVS; Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017; and the 2004 Constitution (Article 71). The EDGE project is also developing additional legal and regulatory frameworks.
revision_notes: Original sources fetched and read, confirming the framework of Decree 11/2008, Decree 44/2010 (NUIC), Civil Registration Code 12/2018 and the Electronic Transactions Law 3/2017. A fresh search identified the more recent and more specific Law No. 6/2022 (approved by the Assembleia da Republica, 20 June 2022), which updates Decree 11/2008 and introduces an integrated data-storage circuit and optical reading zone to the BI, and its implementing decree approved by the Council of Ministers on 2 June 2026. Formal legislation clearly governs digital identity; score of 2 (Yes) confirmed and strengthened with the newer legal instrument.
revised_comments: A formal legal framework governs digital identity across several instruments: Decree No.11/2008 (biometric identity card), Decree 44/2010 (Unique Citizen Identification Number, NUIC), the Civil Registration Code 12/2018, the Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017, and the 2004 Constitution (Article 71). Law No. 6/2022 (20 June 2022) further updates the civil identification and BI regime, introducing an integrated data-storage circuit and optical reading zone to the credential, with an implementing decree approved by the Council of Ministers in June 2026.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Muhlbauer GmbH (a Bavarian company) holds a PPP concession (awarded 2018, 7-year contract) and established a 60-person local office in Maputo. 800 government staff were trained in all aspects of maintenance and operation, indicating partial in-country capacity. The system is operated under a public-private partnership model with extensive know-how transfer to Mozambican staff, but Muhlbauer retains technical lead. The EDGE project is further building institutional capacity.
revision_notes: All three sources fetched and read. Confirms Muhlbauer GmbH holds the 2018 PPP concession (eight-year contract per the 2024 ID4Africa presentation), maintains a 60-person Maputo office, and 800 government staff have been trained in system maintenance and operation. The vendor remains the technical lead through at least 2026, so in-country capacity is real but partial. Score of 2 (Partial in-country capacity) confirmed.
revised_comments: In-country technical capacity is partial. Muhlbauer ID Services GmbH holds an eight-year public-private partnership concession (from 2018) to build, distribute and support the national ID and travel-document system, and maintains a 60-person office in Maputo. Around 800 government staff have been trained in system maintenance and operation, indicating meaningful technology transfer, but Muhlbauer continues to hold the primary technical and vendor role.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) captures fingerprint data as confirmed by the Wikipedia description of the card and multiple sources. The Muhlbauer system supports fingerprint AFIS. SIM card registration (Decree 12/2023) requires both fingerprints and facial recognition, but the foundational national ID card collects fingerprints only. No confirmed iris collection for the national ID.
revision_notes: All three sources fetched and read. The BI records a fingerprint field per its physical description, and the Muhlbauer system supports fingerprint-based AFIS matching, but neither source explicitly confirms whether a facial image is also captured for the BI itself (the 360 Mozambique article describes fingerprint plus facial capture for SIM registration under a separate 2023 telecoms decree, not for the BI). No stronger primary source (e.g. a DNIC technical specification) was found confirming or ruling out facial capture for the BI. Score of 2 (Fingerprints only) confirmed, though the underlying evidence is thin.
revised_comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) enrolment process is understood to capture fingerprint biometric data, supported by fingerprint-based Automated Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS) matching in the Muhlbauer-built system. No confirmed iris or facial-image capture for the BI itself has been documented; facial recognition alongside fingerprints is instead required separately for SIM card registration under Decree 12/2023.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The Muhlbauer system (implemented 2018-2019) provides a nationwide digital system for issuing ID cards and travel documents, distributed to 12 provinces and 177 districts with central databases. The e-CRVS system since 2018 registers births/deaths electronically. The Muhlbauer contract established four interlinked digital databases (citizen data, foreigner data, travel documents, border management). The national ID system is digital end-to-end.
revision_notes: All sources fetched and read. The Muhlbauer system (deployed 2018-2019) provides four interlinked, nationwide electronic databases (citizen, foreigner, travel document, border management), distributed to all provinces and district offices; the 2024 ID4Africa presentation confirms over 6.4 million national eIDs issued digitally between January 2019 and March 2024. Records are digital end-to-end. Score of 3 (Digital) confirmed.
revised_comments: Identity records are stored electronically. The nationwide Muhlbauer-built system, deployed from 2018-2019, comprises four interlinked digital databases (citizen, foreigner, travel document and border management) distributed across all provinces and district offices, with more than 6.4 million national eIDs issued digitally by March 2024. The e-CRVS system similarly registers births and deaths electronically.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Mozambique has a partially deployed biometric national ID system. The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) is issued nationally by DNIC/SNIC under Decree No.11/2008 via the Muhlbauer-built system (PPP contract 2018). Civil registration uses the e-CRVS system. However, as of 2023 coverage is ~52.9% of population and the system lacks full interoperability across agencies. The World Bank EDGE project ($150M, 2021) is actively supporting expansion. Three separate agencies manage civil registration, NID, and immigration.
revision_notes: Sources fetched and read. Confirms the BI is issued nationally under Decree 11/2008 via the Muhlbauer-built system (PPP since 2018); by March 2024 over 6.4 million eIDs had been issued (ID4Africa), while IOM data reported in June 2024 put adult ID-card coverage at only 34%. The World Bank's $150m EDGE project is actively expanding coverage through a nationwide free-issuance campaign (ongoing into 2026). Coverage remains well short of universal and interoperability across agencies is limited. Score of 4 (Partially deployed) confirmed.
revised_comments: Mozambique operates a partially deployed biometric national ID system. The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) is issued nationwide by DNIC under Decree No.11/2008 via a Muhlbauer-built system in place since 2018, with over 6.4 million national eIDs issued by March 2024. Adult coverage nonetheless remains around one-third of the population, according to IOM data reported in mid-2024, and civil registration, national ID and immigration continue to be managed by three separate agencies with limited interoperability. The World Bank-backed EDGE project is actively expanding coverage through an ongoing nationwide free-issuance campaign.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Mozambique lacks a fully operational interoperability framework. The World Bank EDGE project PID (2021) explicitly states 'the absence of an operational interoperability framework leads to wasteful duplication of efforts.' Civil registration, national ID, and immigration are managed by three separate agencies with limited coordination. The Muhlbauer system has four independently operable databases that are interlinked, but government-wide interoperability remains absent. INAGE was created to manage the interoperability platform but is not yet operational.
revision_notes: All sources fetched and read. The 2021 World Bank PID states explicitly that 'the absence of an operational interoperability framework leads to wasteful duplication of efforts.' A June 2025 UNECA inception report on Mozambique's data governance strategy confirms a 'critical need for interoperability and secure data sharing' persists as a core challenge, with coordination gaps between INTIC, INAGE and INCM. Score of 1 (No) confirmed with fresher evidence.
revised_comments: The digital ID system is not yet interoperable across government agencies. Civil registration, national ID and immigration remain managed by three separate agencies with limited coordination, and a June 2025 review of Mozambique's data governance found continuing gaps in inter-institutional data sharing and no operational interoperability framework. The National Institute of Electronic Government (INAGE) has been tasked with developing an interoperability platform, but this is not yet functional.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade historically had a fee (90 MTs for under-18, 180 MTs for over-18 per the Global Protection Cluster briefing note). However, since November 2023, DNIC launched a nationwide free ID campaign for all new registrations, supported by the World Bank EDGE project. The World Bank feature article (July 2024) confirms 140,000 IDs were delivered free of charge. As of 2023-2024, new ID registration is free under the campaign, though renewal and replacement may still carry costs.
revision_notes: All five sources fetched and read. World Bank and Biometric Update sources (2024) confirm a free first-issuance campaign launched November 2023; AIM (May 2026) confirms the DNIC issued 158,560 free BIs in the 'campanha de primeira emissao gratuita' in Q1 2026 alone, and checka.co.mz (March 2026) confirms the government's free registration drive (World Bank-funded, targeting 7 million people by December 2026) covers first-time registration, birth certificates and first BI issuance for all ages. However, a separate checka.co.mz consumer guide (April 2026) lists standard DNIC fees of 90 MT (under 18) and 180 MT (18+) for BI issuance/renewal, indicating the standard channel still charges a fee outside the targeted free campaign. Evidence is therefore mixed: a large, ongoing, government/World Bank-funded free-issuance campaign coexists with a fee-based standard process. This does not map cleanly onto a binary Yes/No score and is flagged for human review rather than asserted either way.
revised_comments: Credential cost is mixed. The standard DNIC fee schedule charges 90 meticais for applicants under 18 and 180 meticais for those 18 and over. In parallel, the government has run a World Bank-supported free-issuance campaign since November 2023 - expanded in March 2026 into a nationwide drive targeting around seven million citizens without prior documentation by December 2026 - under which registration, birth certificates and the first BI are provided free of charge; the DNIC reported issuing 158,560 free BIs under this campaign in the first quarter of 2026 alone.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Mozambique is a member of SADC (Southern African Development Community). SADC citizens do not need a visa to enter Mozambique, but cross-border travel requires a passport (not the national BI card) per accommodation/border post documentation. SADC has regional frameworks for identity document recognition. There is no confirmed formal SADC digital identity interoperability mechanism, but the Mozambican BI is recognized within some regional contexts. The Muhlbauer border management system supports ICAO-compliant travel document verification.
revision_notes: Original two sources re-checked plus three fresh sources fetched and read. The SADC Protocol on the Facilitation of Movement of Persons (2005) defines the 'travel document' used for cross-border entry as a passport (or laissez-passer/border pass), not a national ID card. Independent, current border-crossing guides for Mozambique (accommodationmozambique.co.za; mozambiqueexpert.com) both confirm SADC residents require a valid passport, not the Bilhete de Identidade, to enter or exit Mozambique. No source was found confirming a bilateral or SADC-wide agreement recognising Mozambique's BI as a travel document (unlike, for example, the 2019 Namibia-Botswana ID arrangement). The original score of 2 ('recognised in some regional contexts') is not supported by the evidence gathered; it also mis-cited an ECOWAS example, which is not relevant to Mozambique's SADC membership. Revised to 1 (No).
revised_comments: The Bilhete de Identidade is not recognised as a cross-border travel document. Mozambique is a member of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), whose Protocol on the Facilitation of Movement of Persons defines the relevant travel document as a passport, and current border-crossing guidance confirms SADC citizens require a valid passport - not the national ID card - to enter or exit Mozambique. No bilateral or regional agreement recognising the BI itself for cross-border travel has been identified.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade is typically issued to individuals 18 years of age and older (the Wikipedia article and Global Protection Cluster briefing confirm costs for under-18 and over-18 categories). The application requires a birth certificate. The BI is valid 5 years for those under 40, 10 years for those 40-50, and for life after 50. While children under 18 can technically apply, the standard eligibility threshold for the national biometric ID card is 18+. The NUIC is assigned at birth for civil registration purposes.
revision_notes: Fresh sources fetched and read. The DNIC spokesperson, quoted by the national news agency AIM (May 2026), states the BI 'pode ser emitido desde o nascimento' (can be issued from birth). The Mozambican Embassy in Brasilia's official guidance similarly describes the BI as 'atribuido a nascenca' (assigned at birth). This directly contradicts the original assumption, drawn from a Wikipedia stub and a 2021 briefing note, that 18 is the standard eligibility threshold; those sources in fact only described differentiated fees for under/over-18 applicants, not a minimum enrolment age. Revised to 5 (<1), reflecting that registration is possible from birth.
revised_comments: Registration for the national ID is possible from birth; the Direccao Nacional de Identificacao Civil (DNIC) confirms the Bilhete de Identidade can be issued from birth, linked to the Unique Citizen Identification Number (NUIC) assigned at birth registration, and Mozambican consular guidance similarly describes the credential as attributed at birth. Differentiated processing fees apply for applicants under and over 18 years of age, but this reflects pricing rather than a minimum eligibility age.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) enrollment is not mandatory under Mozambican law. Wikipedia's list of national identity card policies indicates 'N/A' for Mozambique (not compulsory). The low coverage rate (~34-52% of adults) is consistent with optional enrollment. Citizens use voter cards and other documents as alternative identification. The World Bank and government are encouraging uptake through free ID campaigns but have not mandated enrollment.
revision_notes: Original two sources re-checked; Wikipedia's cross-country list still records Mozambique as non-compulsory ('N/A'), and IOM data reported by AIM in June 2024 found only 34% of adults hold a BI, consistent with a system that is not being enforced as compulsory. However, a fresh AIM article (May 2026) directly quotes a DNIC spokesperson stating the BI 'torna-se obrigatorio a partir dos seis anos de idade' (becomes mandatory from age six). This is a single, if authoritative, source directly contradicting the low-coverage evidence and Wikipedia's classification, and it is unclear whether it reflects an actual legal mandate (e.g. under Law 6/2022) or an aspirational/administrative statement. This conflict is not resolved by the evidence gathered and is flagged for human review rather than asserting either 'Optional' or 'Mandatory for all'.
revised_comments: The mandatory status of BI enrolment is unclear from available evidence. Historical sources classify enrolment as non-compulsory, consistent with adult ID-card coverage of only around 34% reported in 2024. However, a DNIC spokesperson stated in May 2026 that the BI becomes obligatory from the age of six, which would indicate a legal or administrative mandate not reflected in older sources or in current coverage levels.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The BI is accepted for healthcare access. CIPESA notes the NUIC is used on 'health cards' in Mozambique. The Global Protection Cluster briefing note (2021) lists healthcare among services requiring ID. The World Bank blog (2023) confirms 'lack of identification prevents access to... health services.' The EDGE/NCRP project enabled IDPs to access 'health' services through ID issuance. However, healthcare access does not appear to be strictly mandatorily gated by the national ID - ID is accepted/beneficial but not universally required.
revision_notes: All three sources fetched and read; confirm the BI is used on health cards and accepted for accessing health services but is not a strict precondition, particularly in humanitarian/emergency contexts for displaced people. Score of 2 (Accepted but not mandatory) confirmed.
revised_comments: The BI is accepted, though not strictly mandatory, for accessing public healthcare services. The Unique Citizen Identification Number (NUIC) is also used on health cards, and displaced persons assisted through the EDGE/NCRP programme have used ID issuance to access health services alongside other services. In emergency contexts for internally displaced people, however, possession of an ID is not treated as a strict precondition for receiving basic services.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Some non-nationals are eligible for identity documents. The Muhlbauer system issues 'resident alien cards' and biometric emergency travel documents for foreigners.
